plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disk. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, and the plant is grown widely for oil, seeds, and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated across Europe, Russia, Ukraine, the United States, and Argentina
plants.funFact: Sunflower heads are not single flowers but composite inflorescences containing up to 2,000 tiny florets arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a magnet for bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer, peaking July to August, with some late flowering into September
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; widely grown in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the Pacific Northwest of the United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years; the name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', since Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Epilobium angustifolium
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower that forms spires of vivid pink-magenta flowers, blooming from the bottom of the spike upward. It quickly colonizes burned or disturbed land across boreal and mountain regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to late summer (July to September)
plants.location: Northern Hemisphere including Alaska, Canada, Scandinavia, Siberia, and the Rocky Mountains
plants.funFact: Locals say that when fireweed blooms reach the top of the stalk, summer is nearly over, since flowering progresses upward as the season advances.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small evergreen tree or large shrub with sickle-shaped phyllodes and fluffy, fragrant golden ball-like flower clusters. It is Australia's national floral emblem and lights up the bush in late winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring in the Southern Hemisphere (July to October)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia including Victoria, New South Wales, South Australia, and Tasmania
plants.funFact: Australia celebrates National Wattle Day on September 1, and the golden and green of the wattle inspired the country's national sporting colors.
